title: Customer financial requests orchestration & prioritization guidelines
creator: Asha Patel
description: Summary: We need a lightweight, repeatable orchestration and prioritization process for incoming enterprise requests related to pricing, commitments, invoicing, cost allocation, and marketplace billing. These requests currently land via Sales, Support, and Solutions Engineering with inconsistent detail and inconsistent routing which causes delay and rework. Goals: 1) reduce mean time to decision for enterprise financial requests to under 5 business days for triage + initial owner assignment, 2) provide a consistent rubric so that engineering and finance can prioritize work by revenue impact, legal complexity, and implementation effort, 3) centralize artifacts (templates and decision logs) to speed handoffs and audits.
problem_statement: High-variance intake causes missed SLAs and untracked one-off billing adjustments. Engineering gets ad-hoc asks for invoice adjustments and marketplace flow fixes without clear business impact or approved terms. Sales expects fast answers on commitments/discounts but Finance needs auditable decisions. We need a single source-of-truth triage process that balances speed and controls.
proposed_solution: 1) Build a triage intake form (Sales/Solutions/Support) with mandatory fields (customer ARR, contract ID, requested outcome, deadline, marketplace channel, whether credits/invoice adjustments are required). 2) Create a 4-axis decision rubric: Revenue Impact, Compliance Risk, Implementation Effort, Reusability. 3) Define owner routing rules: Finance handles invoicing adjustments & marketplace billing disputes; PM handles packaging/price policy changes; Eng handles runtime/metric changes. 4) SLA & lifecycle states (Submitted -> Triage -> Owner Assigned -> Proposal -> Approved -> Implementation -> Closed). 5) Publish a runbook + template email responses and a small ‘fast-track’ process for < $X monthly revenue impact.
tradeoffs_and_considerations: - Fast-track reduces latency but increases risk of inconsistent precedent; require post-hoc audit for fast-track items. - Heavy intake forms reduce re-submissions but increase friction for Sales engineers; use progressive disclosure (minimal required fields up front, optional follow-ups). - Marketplace flows often require cloud vendor involvement which extends timelines; we should flag those and provide expected calendar SLAs.
acceptance_criteria: Triage intake form created in Confluence + form submission endpoint (or Salesforce case template) and validated by Sales Ops.
Decision rubric documented with scoring thresholds and example scenarios for Commitments, Invoicing, Cost Allocation, and Marketplace items.
Routing matrix that maps triage outcomes to a single named owner role (Finance, PM, Eng, Legal) with escalation paths.
SLA definitions: initial triage within 3 business days, owner assignment within 5 business days, fast-track <= 48 hours.
At least two trial runs with active deals (Sales sandbox) and retrospective notes captured in the shared drive.
Templates for customer communications and an audit log file format for Finance to consume.
Instrumented dashboard (in Console or internal sheet) showing number of open requests, avg time-to-owner, and revenue-at-stake per request.
implementation_steps: Draft intake form fields and minimal validation - owner: Liam Chen

Create decision rubric doc and example scoring - owner: PM team
Implement routing matrix and Slack notifications for new submissions - owner: Eng Operations
Run 2 pilot triages with AE deals and collect feedback - owner: Solutions Eng
Iterate on thresholds and publish runbook and templates - owner: PM
Create dashboard (sheet/Console) and add to weekly GTM review - owner: Analytics
risks: Ambiguous revenue thresholds leading to inconsistent approvals
Delays in marketplace vendor responses causing SLA misses
Insufficient audit trail if teams use ad-hoc email instead of the intake form
